terms.gloss: be stuck in, be absorbed in
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, intransitive; with in and the ablative
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.40.2: equidem in librīs haereō (Lewis & Short), s.v. haereō
terms.comment: “To stick” to a thing; Cicero, at his books: in librīs haereō. Lewis & Short also cites valdē in scrībendō haereō (Att. 13.39.2), where it is rather “I am stuck”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 99, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
